statusNote: All unknowns answered; kit, tooling, ESLint set, Node minimum and template purpose decided by Zac with evidence and a probe on Ang's code; ADR 0002 amendment noted

knowns.fact: Stance: MIT decided; PR and issue templates wanted (redirect first-principle clashes to 'raise it in your own Ang', plus an open-conversation template); no markdown linting

Kit: ESLint, Prettier, Husky, lint-staged and CI, dev-only at the repo root, with node:test as the test runner (Vitest dropped, see test-runner); Zac's call 2026-11-16 because the code will be read and bears his name
knowns.answers: Is quality tooling for the Ang repo worth it: none, B (zero-dep node --check/--test in CI) or C (dev-only full kit)?

knowns.fact: The test command documented in 10k/technical/project-structure.md runs 0 of 37 tests (Node's glob skips .claude/); fixing it is part of this idea's tooling work: use 'src/.claude/**/*.test.mjs' or a package.json test script

Small whimsical repos keep README+LICENSE (+changelog if versioned), put 'fork it' in the README, mostly drop CoC/SECURITY/CONTRIBUTORS, and use issue templates with blank issues off routing chat to Discussions; three candidate kits for shaping
knowns.answers: Which standards do small, whimsical open-source projects keep, and which suit Ang?

knowns.fact: Tests stay on node:test beside the code and ship with installs (install stream's call); Vitest would make every install need a package. Tooling lives in a private dev-only root package.json; ADR 0002 gets amended to allow it
knowns.answers: How do Vitest tests coexist with tests that ship in src/ (users have no Vitest), and does ADR 0002 need amending for a dev-only root package.json?

knowns.fact: Sane-default ESLint set for plain Node ESM: @eslint/js recommended, eslint-plugin-n flat/recommended-module, eslint-plugin-regexp flat/recommended, eslint-config-prettier/flat last, plus globals; all ESLint 10-ready and probe on Ang's code found only real issues
knowns.answers: Which ESLint plugins does the community treat as sane defaults for plain Node ESM (zero-dep CLI, node:test tests)?

knowns.fact: No: shipped Ang drops the /bootstrap-quality nudge; /bootstrap-repo offers tooling up front, declining is a decision, and /trigger covers reminders (Zac, 2026-11-16)
knowns.answers: Should the generic personal rule still push /bootstrap-quality on repos lacking tooling?

knowns.fact: Node 26 (the current LTS) is the minimum supported version; all 37 tests pass on v26.13.1. Older versions may work but aren't supported
knowns.answers: What minimum Node version does Ang support? Docs say 21+, but the code uses import.meta.dirname, which eslint-plugin-n flags below 22.16; the root package.json engines field must state it

knowns.fact: Templates only, as a guided rubber-ducking nudge toward Ang's first principles, not a guard: no collaborators-only setting, PR cap or auto-close. Evidence shows templates don't block PRs, and blocking was never the aim
knowns.answers: How should Ang guard against agent-written PRs/issues and forkers PR-ing upstream by accident (template wording, collaborators-only settings)?

decisions.decision: Adopt C: lint to zero errors and zero warnings, with auto-fix on (ESLint --fix and Prettier --write on commit); markdown is ignored by every linter and formatter
Go full grown-up repo: status badges on the README (CI and the like), not a minimal look
Sane defaults: Prettier as shipped plus semicolons and trailing commas, set explicitly; ESLint with the style and syntax plugins the community treats as sane defaults
CONTRIBUTING points people to the issue and PR templates and says how to use them; the README links to it
No account-level zacbraddy/.github defaults (kit 3 out): hygiene files live in the Ang repo only, since not every repo needs this rigour and copy-paste suits the few that do (Zac, 2026-11-16)

Kit 2: kit 1 (README 'fork it' section, issue templates with blank issues off, fork-aware PR template, private vulnerability reporting on) plus a short CONTRIBUTING and a short code of conduct in Ang's voice (Zac's preference, 2026-11-16)
Keep node:test, drop Vitest from the kit: shipped tests must run with Node alone in every install, and no test files change (Zac, 2026-11-16)
Root package.json is private and dev-only (ESLint, Prettier, Husky, lint-staged) with npm test = node --test 'src/.claude/**/*.test.mjs'; amend ADR 0002 when it is built

ESLint set: @eslint/js + n (no-process-exit off, prefer-node-protocol on) + regexp + eslint-config-prettier, globals.node; unicorn, jsdoc, security, import(-x), promise and all-in-one configs dropped — too noisy or churny under zero warnings, lagging ESLint 10, or adding nothing on Ang's code

Remove the 'flag it once and suggest /bootstrap-quality' line from the shipped engineering-defaults rule and 'flag that instead' from the bootstrap-quality description — Ang agents don't nag, and one repo's tooling choice binds no other install (Zac, 2026-11-16)

Develop against the current Node LTS and make it the minimum: engines >=26, .node-version 26, CI on 26, bumped together each October; release notes say older versions may work but aren't supported. Only the version we develop on is actually tested (Zac, 2026-11-16)

Templates only (option C), PR and issue alike, as rubber-ducking nudges toward first principles: the PR template asks the raiser to justify the change for all Ang users so ego PRs talk themselves into a local workflow improvement; issues lead with open conversation over cold feature demands, though both are welcome; bad PRs still arriving is accepted (Zac, 2026-11-16)

Releases are git tags with generated GitHub Releases, no hand-kept changelog: install.sh and the upgrade skill pin to tags (install-uninstall-update's install-script spike). Stamping the tag into install.sh before tagging (their u12) stays with that stream (Zac, 2026-11-16)
